source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: What distinguishes hidden recurrence from the autoregressive output loop?

options.text: Hidden recurrence trains weights; autoregression trains embeddings.
options.feedback: Both can describe inference with already trained weights. Their distinction concerns internal processing versus growth of the output sequence.

options.text: Hidden recurrence refines vectors; autoregression extends the sequence.
options.feedback: A recurrent pass can refine numerical representations before selection. Autoregression adds a selected token that shapes subsequent generation.

options.text: Hidden recurrence selects full answers; autoregression selects paragraphs.
options.feedback: Neither mechanism requires selecting a complete answer or paragraph at once. The generation process studied here advances by tokens.

options.text: Hidden recurrence enlarges context limits; autoregression enlarges layers.
options.feedback: Those are capacity and architecture changes. The two loops instead describe what is repeated during processing.
